title: Test process count fits the machine it runs on
what: On a machine with a different core count (or without macOS's first-run scan of new executables), the number of test processes a gate uses, and the number of gate slots, fit that machine instead of the default measured on the owner's Mac.
why: Owner, 27 Oct small hours, on the gate-speed branch 3: "На разных устройствах с разным количеством ядер - будет ли пересчитано эффективное количество процессов ? Не изменяй текущее может добавить это в очередь если необходимо". Facts that night: the design sets RELAY_TEST_JOBS to a fixed default (4, or the knee branch 3 measures on the owner's 12-core Mac) bounded by 1..core count, so a 2-core machine gets 2 but a 32-core machine still gets the Mac's number; the measured caps on the Mac are 12 cores, 3 gate slots and macOS scanning each new executable for ~0.75 s at ~2.7 per second machine-wide (Linux has no such scan). Relay runs on one machine today; other machines come with relay-installs-with-one-command-from-its-own-rep. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
where: the parallel library-test runner (RELAY_TEST_JOBS) from the gate-speed branch 3

fact: 27 Oct, branch wt/gate-slots (not yet merged): gates now take a slot from one per-machine setting in relay's config (default 2 on 12 cores, from the core count) read in lib/relay_gate.py; the name DEFAULT_SLOTS this item refers to changed there. Measured on this Mac, 4 test jobs per gate: one gate alone 420 s, two at once 698 s each, three 1058 s each.
